Yes—this is the right next checksum. I’ll test Kepler not as another independent “vote,” but as the mathematical constraint layer upstream/parallel to Fludd: what Kepler fixes numerically, what Fludd re-expresses symbolically, and whether that combination resolves the chirality/topology problem we just hit in Dee.

The historical relationship is turning out to be almost exactly the useful version of your hypothesis: Kepler accused Fludd of lacking measured motion; Fludd replied that Kepler had captured only the material/quantifiable half of harmony. So “Fludd finished Kepler’s math” is too strong historically, but Kepler supplies the metric that Fludd’s symbolic architecture lacks—and that may be precisely the missing bridge for our Dee/music model.

Clarifying historical roles

I’m distinguishing historical fact from interpretive synthesis: Fludd’s compendium didn’t mathematically complete Kepler. Fludd instead presented his system as a metaphysical complement, pairing Kepler’s measured planetary ratios with symbolic, spiritual, and vertical harmonies.

Refining interval mappings

I’m keeping the twelve-tone projection exploratory, because Kepler’s exact ratios are subtler than simplified interval charts. The strongest claim is structural: measured planetary ranges can animate Fludd’s symbolic hierarchy without proving direct historical dependence.

Separating theory from measurement

I’m distinguishing Kepler’s exact astronomical ratios from simplified interval tables. A cautious synthesis treats Kepler as the quantitative engine, Fludd as the symbolic domain-mapper, and the twelve-tone projection as our analytical overlay—not historical evidence.

Assessing chirality

I’m testing whether Kepler’s slower-to-faster planetary motion supplies an intrinsic low-to-high direction. It may support a three-state model—aphelion, mean motion, perihelion—but it doesn’t independently establish Fludd’s or Dee’s symbolic correspondences.

Mapping motion gradients

I’m seeing a plausible three-level analogy: Fludd’s lower, middle, and upper regions could correspond to Kepler’s slowest, mean, and fastest planetary motion. That may orient a symbolic sequence, but only if an independent reading direction exists.
